entities.summary: Joseph-Marie, comte Portalis was a French diplomat and statesman who played a crucial role in the development of French diplomacy during the early 19th century. He was born into a noble family and received a thorough education, which served him well in his diplomatic career. Portalis served as the French ambassador to Russia from 1813 to 1814, where he played a key role in the Congress of Vienna, which redrew the map of Europe after Napoleon's defeat. He also served as the French minister of foreign affairs from 1823 to 1828, during which time he oversaw the signing of the Treaty of Paris, which ended the First Carlist War. Portalis's diplomatic efforts helped to establish France as a major power in Europe and laid the groundwork for the country's future involvement in international relations. He died on August 5, 1858, and was remembered as a skilled diplomat and statesman who played a significant role in shaping French foreign policy during a tumultuous period in European history.
